 ORDER Heard and perused the record.

This is an appeal filed by appellant under section 14-A(2) of Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.736/2023, dated (not mentioned) registered at Police Station-Kishanganj Mhow, District Indore (MP) for offence under Sections 365, 376, 376(2) (n), 376(d), 506/34 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 and also under Sections 3(2)(W)(ii) and 3(2)(V) of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.

sentences.text: T his appeal under Section 14(A)(2) of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 has been filed against order dated 30.11.2023 passed by Special Judge [under SC/ST(PA) Act] District-Indore in Special Case / Bail Application No.145/2023 whereby learned Special Judge rejected the bail application of appellant.
He is in detention since 04.08.2023 3 .
The allegation against the applicant is that he alongwith co-accused committed rape upon the prosecturix.
4 . Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that the allegation against the applicant is to keep the prosecutrix in forest area, where no one can reach.

He further submits that the incident was happened on 02.02.2023, in between, the prosecutrix has filed the application of Ladli Behna Yojana, if she was kept in such place, how could she, file the appliation of Ladli Behna Yojana.

The another co-accused Ramsingh Rathore and Gopal Singh against whom allegation of rape has been alleged, have been granted bail vide order dated 24.11.2023 and 11.12.2023 by this Court in M.Cr.C.
Nos. 14158/2023 14636/2023.
The appellant is innocent and has not committed any offence.
It is further submitted the prosecutrix and accused Ranjeet were in relationship for a period of approximately two years.
The age of the prosecutrix is about 30 years.
The appellant is in jail since 04.08.2023 i.e. more than four months and final conclusion of trial will take sufficient long time.
Therefore, it has been prayed that the appellant/accused be released on bail, pending the trial.

5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State as well as counsel for the objector have vehemently opposed the prayer and prayed for dismissal of this appeal and submitted that there are criminal cases registered against the applicant.

6. In reply, counsel for the applicant also submits that only on the basis of previous criminal record,
no one can be kept in jail for long period.

7. Having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case and custody period of the appellant as well as co-accused persons have already been granted bail, but without expressing any opinion on the merit of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which further pre-trial detention of the appellant-accused is not warranted.
Consequently, appeal stands allowed.

8. It is directed that appellant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
8.

By way of abundant caution, it is further directed that the applicant shall also mark his presence before the concerned Police Station on 2nd and 4th Money of every month between 10.00 am to 12.00 noon during pendency of the trial.

Any default in attendance in court and marking presence in the concerned police station, would result in cancellation of bail granted by this Court thereby entitling the police to take the applicant in custody immediately.
9. This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case o f bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
